name: CAMEROON

flag.title: Tricolour & Star
flag.note: Green, red, yellow with gold star

lead: Cameroon sits where Africa's regions meet. Rainforest meets savanna, and a volcano rises straight from the sea. People speak 280 languages. Geographers call it "Africa in miniature" because desert, jungle, highlands and coast all fit inside one country.
geo: Cameroon is shaped like an upside-down triangle. The south is dense rainforest. The centre rises to cool highlands. The north flattens into grassland near Lake Chad.
Mount Cameroon, an active volcano, rises straight from the sea. The remote Dja Forest is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and one of Africa's best-kept rainforests.
animals: Western lowland gorillas, forest elephants and chimpanzees live in the rainforests. Drills, big monkeys with bright faces, live only here and on nearby Bioko Island.
Birdwatchers visit the Cameroon Highlands to see 20+ birds found nowhere else on Earth. One is Bannerman's turaco, with bright red wings. Leatherback turtles nest on Atlantic beaches.
culture: More than 280 ethnic groups live in Cameroon, including Bamileke, Fulani, Beti and Bassa. The Bamileke dance in elephant masks. Huge carved headdresses sway to thundering drums.
Ndólé is a stew of bitter leaves and groundnuts. Football is a national love. The Indomitable Lions have won the Africa Cup of Nations five times.
history: Portuguese sailors arrived in 1472. They named the Wouri River 'Rio dos Camarões' (River of Prawns), and that gave the country its name. Germany colonised the area in 1884.
After World War I, Britain and France split the land. French Cameroun became independent on 1 January 1960. The British part joined in 1961 to make today's bilingual republic.
wows: Mount Cameroon is the tallest peak in West-Central Africa.
Cameroon has over 280 languages, one of the most per km² on Earth.
Debundscha gets about 10,000 mm of rain a year.
In 1990, the Indomitable Lions became the first African team in a World Cup quarter-final.
Cameroon plays two national anthems at official events, in French and English.
Lake Nyos released a deadly CO₂ cloud in 1986, a rare limnic eruption.
At the Ngondo festival, a diver takes messages to river spirits.

myths.fact: Cameroonian Pidgin is a real language with its own grammar. Millions of people speak it every day.

myths.myth: Mother sea turtles guard their eggs
myths.fact: Mothers bury the eggs and swim away. The babies hatch alone and race to the sea.
